final_answer: Yes. In the provided ATAC-seq peak calls, AI-10-49 treatment is associated with global chromatin-accessibility remodeling in ME-1 inv(16) AML cells. Compared with DMSO, AI-10-49 samples had fewer called ATAC peaks overall (mean 50,923.5 vs 65,997.5 peaks; about 23% fewer, and 11,933 vs 26,528 peaks per million filtered fragments), indicating a net contraction of the accessible peak repertoire. However, the peaks present after treatment were globally stronger and broader: pooled median MACS2 signalValue increased from 5.317 to 6.795, median -log10(q) from 5.105 to 7.444, and median peak width from 103 bp to 118 bp. A consensus-union analysis also showed condition-specific remodeling: 37.97% of union regions were DMSO-only, 12.85% were AI-10-49-only, and 4,801 regions were present in both DMSO replicates but absent from both AI-10-49 replicates, versus 2,007 showing the opposite pattern. Overall, the data support a global accessibility shift after AI-10-49, dominated by loss of many accessible sites together with stronger and broader residual accessible regions, rather than a simple uniform genome-wide increase.
